questions.context: Clase de ingles de sexto grado en la que se repasa cuando usar How much y How many.

options.text: How much books do you have?
options.feedback: how much is used with uncountable nouns, and books is a countable noun.

options.text: How many books do you have?
options.feedback: how many is used with countable nouns, and books can be counted, so the question is correct.
That structure with are goes with uncountable nouns such as money or water.
The question mixes how many with an uncountable noun and its verb is the wrong choice.

questions.explanation: La eleccion entre how much y how many depende de una sola pregunta: se puede contar el sustantivo con numeros. Los libros se cuentan, la moneda no, y esa comprobacion resuelve practicamente todos los casos de la unidad.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question: "___ sugar do you need?"
questions.context: Ejercicio de compra en la tienda de la esquina.

options.feedback: how many cannot go before sugar because the units of sugar are not counted.
how much goes before uncountable nouns such as sugar, water or milk.
how long asks for a length of time, not for a quantity.
how old asks for an age and has nothing to do with a quantity.

questions.explanation: Los sustantivos incontables en inglesExpressan la cantidad con una unidad de medida en lugar de con un numeral. Por eso se dice how much sugar pero two kilos of sugar, y mezclar ambas estructuras es el error habitual.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "We need some rice, some milk and two cans of tuna." What can be counted?
questions.context: Lectura de un aviso sobre la donacion de alimentos a un banco de alimentos.

options.feedback: Cans of tuna takes the numeral two, which shows that the cans are counted.
Rice goes with some and with a unit of weight, and not with a direct numeral.
Milk is uncountable and therefore does not accept a numeral such as two.
The text allows you to separate what is counted from what is not, and that generality does not answer the question.

questions.explanation: Identificar en el texto que elementos aparecen con numeral y cuales con some o some mucho permite deducir la regla sin necesidad de explicarla de antemano. Esa observacion inductiva es la que consolida el criterio de contable e incontable.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the right quantifier for a plural countable subject?
questions.context: Ejercicio de descripcion de una habitacion en el examen de grado sexto.

options.text: There aren't much chairs in the room.
options.feedback: chairs is countable, so the plural quantifier many is required and much cannot go before it.

options.text: There aren't many chairs in the room.
options.feedback: Chairs is countable, so the negative quantifier is many and the sentence becomes aren't many chairs.

options.text: There aren't many chair in the room.
options.feedback: The noun chair is in the singular and does not agree with the plural are.

options.text: There isn't much chairs in the room.
options.feedback: That option combines the singular verb isn't with a plural noun, and it also uses much with a countable noun.

questions.explanation: En la negacion many y much anteponen el verbo al sustantivo, y por eso el orden de la oracion cambia respecto a la afirmativa. Revisar a la vez la concordancia del verbo y el criterio contable resuelve las tres errores en una sola comprobacion.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "A sandwich costs three dollars and a juice costs two dollars." How much does a sandwich cost?
questions.context: Ejercicio de lectura de precios en un menu de cafeteria escolar.

options.feedback: The text says literally that the sandwich costs three dollars.
Two dollars is the price of the juice and not of the sandwich.
Five dollars would be the sum of the two prices, and the question asks for one only.
One dollar does not appear in the text as the price of any item.

questions.explanation: Cuando un texto presenta dos precios y la pregunta pide solo uno, el riesgo mayor es sumar. Localizar la palabra clave sandwich en la pregunta y buscarla en el texto evita esa confusion de manera inmediata.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "___ students are in the library this morning."
questions.context: Ejercicio de escritura de un anuncio para el tablón del salon.

options.feedback: much does not accept a countable plural noun such as students.
many goes before countable nouns in the plural, and students is one of them.
long qualifies nouns and does not go in front of a noun such as students.
little goes before uncountable nouns and is used in negative sentences.

questions.explanation: Los cuantificadores del ingles tienen restricciones de categoria: many con contables plurales, much con incontables, little con incontables en negativo y few con contables en negativo. Conocer esa tabla evita casi todos los errores de la unidad.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Reflexion sobre el uso de los cuantificadores poco y mucho.

options.text: There is little water in the bottle.
options.feedback: That sentence would be correct in Spanish, but in English little is used in the negative.

options.text: There isn't much water in the bottle.
options.feedback: much is the quantifier that goes with uncountable nouns in the negative.

options.text: There aren't little students in the class.
options.feedback: little does not go before countable nouns such as students.

options.text: There is a little book in the desk.
options.feedback: a little does go before a countable singular noun, but the question asks for the form little.

questions.explanation: En ingles a little admite un sustantivo singular contable, pero little a secas solo aparece en frases negativas. El enunciado pide justamente la forma little, y por eso la unica respuesta que la contiene de manera correcta es la opcion B.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Translate to English: "Hay mucha gente en el parque."
questions.context: Ejercicio de traduccion de un aviso escolar del espanol al ingles.

options.text: There are many people at the park.
options.feedback: People is countable because it accepts the numerals one person and two people, so it needs many.

options.text: There is many people at the park.
options.feedback: The verb is does not agree with the plural subject people.

options.text: There are much people at the park.
options.feedback: much is used with uncountables and people is a countable noun.

options.text: There are a lot of people at the park.
options.feedback: a lot of accepts both countable and uncountable nouns, so it works with people.

questions.explanation: People es un sustantivo peculiar porque es plural en forma pero se puede contar con one person. Esa caracteristica hace que many sea la opcion natural, y a lot of es la alternativa equally valida cuando no se quiere insistir en la cantidad exacta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "You should drink two litres of water every day." How much water is recommended?
questions.context: Ejercicio de lectura de un articulo sobre el consumo responsable de agua.

options.feedback: The text speaks of litres and not of bottles, so that unit does not appear in the original.
The text indicates two litres of water, which is exactly the amount recommended.
The substance is water and the text does not mention milk.
One litre would be half the amount the article recommends.

questions.explanation: Los incontables se expresan con la unidad delante del sustantivo, como two litres of water, y no con el sustantivo en plural. Reconocer que el agua no tiene forma plural es lo que permite descartar la opcion de la leche y entender la estructura completa.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question asks for the price correctly?
questions.context: Prueba corta de la unidad para cerrar el trimestre.

options.feedback: how many is used with countable nouns, and the question is looking for a price, not a quantity.
The verb are does not agree with the singular subject the bag.
To ask for the price of an object you use how much with the verb to be.
how old asks for an age and not for the purchase price.

questions.explanation: Cuando how much acompana al verbo to be, la pregunta pide un precio y el sustantivo puede ser contable o incontables. Esa combinacion es la que se usa en las tiendas y es diferente de how much are para sustantivos incontables en plural.
questions.subject: ingles
